Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

I’m fine phrase

also we’re fine, fine, I’m okay, we’re okay, I’m alright, alright, we’re O.K., very well, I’m very well, fine, thanks, in great shape, as well as ever, all’s well at home, everyone’s well, I feel fine

classical

Traupman 15, 17–18

Valeō.

Other words

  • Bene mihi est.

    also used · classical · Traupman 15, 17–18; Traupman 314

  • Mē bene habeō.

    also used · classical · Traupman 15, 17–18; Traupman 314

  • Bene habēmus. — we’re fine

    also used · classical · Traupman 105

  • Rēctē. — fine, all right (as an answer)

    also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 5.5.3: Quid fit? quid agitur? — Rēctē. (Lewis & Short s.v. regō); Traupman 17: fine, rēctē; Traupman 315

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.)

    Lewis & Short: “esp. in answers, in colloquial lang., well, quite well, right”; also a politely evasive “it’s all right, nothing’s the matter” (Plaut. Merc. 2.3.33: Rēctē, pater).

  • Rēctē valeō. — I’m very well

    also used · classical · Plaut. Bacch. 2.2.11: Rēctē valet? — Vīvit rēctē et valet. (Lewis & Short s.v. regō); Plaut. Am. 2.1.36: equidem valeō rēctē et salvus sum (Lewis & Short s.v. valeō); Traupman 17: to be very well, rēctē valēre; Traupman 305

  • Bellē. — fine, very well

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 12.37: bellē sē habēre (Lewis & Short s.v. bellus); Cic. Fam. 9.9.1: bellē habēre, to be in good health (Lewis & Short); Traupman 17: fine, bellē

    The word of Cicero’s letters for being well; the superlative too: bellissimē esse (Cic. Att. 14.14.1, Lewis & Short). Traupman 17 adds Bellissimē and Perbellē, very well; Lewis & Short has perbellē “very finely” (Cic. Fam. 16.18.1) but not of health.

  • Pulchrē est mihi. — I’m well, things are going well for me

    also used · classical · Cic. N. D. 1.114; Hor. S. 2.8.19; Catull. 23.5 (Lewis & Short s.v. pulcher)

    Impersonal, with the person in the dative: “it is fine for me”.

Examples

  • «Rēctēne advēnistis?» inquit avia. «Bene habēmus,» inquit pater.

    “Did you have a good journey?” said Grandma. “We’re fine,” said Dad.Libellus I, Iter in Lūsitāniam

  • Sīc valet ut numquam melius.

    He’s as well as ever.Traupman 15

  • Omnēs domī bene sē habent.

    Everyone at home is well.Traupman 15

  • In optimō statū.

    In great shape.Traupman 18

  • Em, vīvō.

    Well, I’m still alive.Traupman 18

  • Bene valeō.

    I’m fine.Traupman 146

  • Rēctē est.

    Everything’s fine.Traupman 315

See also how are you?, not bad, so far so good.
